action_items: REGRESSION BUG FIXED by me — `_check_player_against_tournament` was defined *twice* (once at module-level in routes/tournaments.py with 2-arg signature, and once imported from core/helpers.py with 3-arg signature supporting M1-C guest quotas). The local module-level shadow won at import time, so the call site at routes/tournaments.py:203 crashed with `TypeError: takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given` on every POST /squads/{id}/players. I removed the shadow. The imported helper (which enforces M1-C guest sub-type quotas via GUEST_QUOTA_PER_SQUAD) is now active. Confirmed via re-running captain_uniqueness test.

Pre-existing test files test_phase4_players.py and test_phase4_2_tournaments.py have hard-coded seed counts (`==15 tournaments`, `==7 players`) that are stale after M1-A/M2-A additive seeding. 14 of 18 failures in those older suites are drift-only (`==15 → 37`, `==4 T20 → 11`, etc.). Please update those hard-coded counts to ≥ thresholds or refactor to use fiscal_cycle filters.

Cosmetic: React `<span> cannot be a child of <option>` hydration warning printed on Players + Tournaments pages — some visual-editor wrapper is emitting a <span> inside <option> elements. Suggest suppressing in production.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/tournaments.py:155-169 (now removed) — a stale local copy of _check_player_against_tournament was silently shadowing the imported (M1-C-aware) version, disabling guest-quota enforcement AND crashing new-squad-player POSTs. Root cause: someone updated the helper in core/helpers.py to accept a 3rd arg (existing_squad_members) for M1-C but forgot to delete the earlier local copy in routes/tournaments.py. Adding a sentinel comment or a lint rule to catch same-name def/import shadows would prevent recurrence.

routes/players.py::get_player() cannot look up by player_display_id when the display id contains '/' (which it always does, e.g. `2026/15-11-99/0001`). Path variables are split on '/' so the API returns 404. If the frontend or public /verify page ever tries to GET by display id, that will fail. Either add an alternate flat-id lookup route (POST /players/lookup or GET /players?display_id=…) or slugify the id (replace '/' with '-'). My test explicitly URL-encodes it — depending on ingress config, %2F may or may not survive routing.

core/helpers.py::_next_fixture_no counts ALL fixtures across cycles (`db.fixtures.count_documents({})`) but formats the serial under the passed cycle prefix. Two cycles running concurrently will collide once fixtures accumulate. Should count where fiscal_cycle == cycle OR where fixture_no.startswith(f'FX-{cycle}').

core/helpers.py::_new_player_display_id — serial derived from `count_documents({'first_registration_year': year})+1` is NOT concurrency-safe. Two concurrent registrations in the same year race to the same serial. Consider a Mongo atomic counter (findAndModify on a `counters` collection).

routes/tournaments.py::submit-for-approval / approve / reject take `actor_name`, `actor_body_id` etc. as query parameters instead of a JSON body. The Player review endpoints take a JSON body (`PlayerReviewAction`). Inconsistent API surface; standardise on JSON body.

routes/tournaments.py::approve — allows Draft → Upcoming *without* going through Awaiting_Approval; effectively bypassing the approval-chain step-1 record. Should require submit-for-approval first (allow only Awaiting_Approval → Upcoming), and add a separate 'auto-approve' path if truly needed.

routes/fixtures.py::log_work_hours accepts negative `hours` (no lower bound) and does not update by absolute value. A malicious/typo negative value silently reduces the accumulated total. Validate hours > 0.

routes/fixtures.py::set_fixture_status is anonymous — no actor recorded on transitions (unlike PlayerAuditEvent). Add a minimal audit trail on Fixture too, especially for Cancelled/Abandoned which are financially material.

Player audit_trail could grow unboundedly on an active roster (one row per doc verify, per patch, per notification). Consider archiving events older than N days into a sibling collection, or capping to last 500.

PlayerCreate accepts `documents` at creation time but create_player() doesn't persist that list (only PlayerBase fields go through **payload.model_dump(); documents is on PlayerCreate). The extra=ignore ConfigDict masks this silently. Either wire documents through or drop the field from PlayerCreate.

GUEST_QUOTA_PER_SQUAD 'Education' entry has junior:1, senior:1, total:1 — the sub-totals sum to 2 but total is capped at 1, which is confusing. If total is the truth, junior/senior sub-caps are dead code; consider removing them.

rca of the issue: Bug: POST /api/squads/{id}/players 500ed with `TypeError: _check_player_against_tournament() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`. Root cause: routes/tournaments.py had a MODULE-LEVEL redefinition of _check_player_against_tournament (2-arg signature, no M1-C quota logic) that ran AFTER the top-of-file `from core.helpers import _check_player_against_tournament` and rebound the name. So when line 203 called the imported symbol expecting 3 args (player, tournament, squad_members) it actually invoked the 2-arg local shadow. Fix: deleted the local shadow. Now the M1-C-aware helper from core.helpers is used, restoring both squad-player creation and the guest-sub-type quota enforcement that M1-C introduced. Verified by pytest test_captain_uniqueness passing after fix. Reproduction: seed the DB, then `curl -X POST /api/squads/{any_valid_squad_id}/players -d '{"player_id":"..."}'` prior to the fix → 500; after fix → 200/400 (as per business rules).
